description: QM derivation with NO E₀ initialization. Null control: tests whether R̄ decrease is merely a context window effect or specific to E₀ priming.
test_prompts:
Derivation Step 1: Complex-valued state spaces.
Using only the E₀ primitives (State, Difference, Path, Resistance, Historization, Time, Rate) and Axiom A₀, derive why states in a fundamental physical theory must be representable as complex-valued (elements of ℂ or a Hilbert space over ℂ). Do not assume any quantum mechanics. Begin from the structural requirements of the primitives alone.

Derivation Step 2: Superposition.
Continuing from the complex-valued state space just derived, now show why the principle of superposition must hold. Using only E₀ primitives and the structural framework already established, derive that if |ψ₁⟩ and |ψ₂⟩ are admissible states, then α|ψ₁⟩ + β|ψ₂⟩ must also be an admissible state. Justify this structurally, not by postulate.

Derivation Step 3: The Born rule.
Continuing from superposition, now derive the Born rule: that the probability of measuring outcome k is P(k) = |α_k|². Using only E₀ primitives and the structural results already established, show why probability must arise as the squared modulus of complex amplitudes. This should follow from structural necessity, not be assumed.

Derivation Step 4: Unitary time evolution.
Continuing from the previous derivations, now derive that time evolution must be unitary. Using E₀ primitives — particularly Historization (non-invertibility of realized transitions) and Rate (v = Δ/R) — show that the evolution operator U(t) must satisfy U†U = I. Connect this to the structural requirement that total difference is conserved under admissible transitions.
